title: The TUI: bootstrap tui and bootstrap mac tui

keeps.check: Build the engine from the worktree (`cd cli && go build -o <tmp>/bootstrap ./cmd/bootstrap`). In a copy of the main checkout of this repository (with its .git), run `env -u MISE_PROJECT_ROOT -u MACOS_SETUP_REPO_PATH BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG=/nonexistent <tmp>/bootstrap tui --clone <worktree> </dev/null`, then the same with `mac tui`.
keeps.pass: Each exits with code 2, prints no TUI screen, and names the hint of D7 (g).

keeps.check: Build the engine from main before this plan (`git -C <main checkout> worktree add --detach <tmp2> main`, then `cd <tmp2>/cli && go build -o <tmp>/bootstrap-old ./cmd/bootstrap`). In two copies of the main checkout of this repository, run `env -u MISE_PROJECT_ROOT -u MACOS_SETUP_REPO_PATH BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG=/nonexistent <bin> init --no-tui --dry-run --clone <worktree> </dev/null`, one with each binary. Remove <tmp2> with git worktree remove after.
keeps.pass: The two outputs and the two exit codes are the same.

after_landing.notes: Archive the plan folder, only when its gaps list has no open entry. With an open gap, skip this step and report the gaps.

decisions.decision: Lip Gloss v2 for the styles.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13): the TUI uses Lip Gloss v2 (charm.land/lipgloss/v2) for the styles, the colors and the layout of the panes, with Bubble Tea v2 and Bubbles v2 of plan 2026-11-12-catalog-engine. U1 adds it with go get at the latest v2 release at the run; go.sum comes from go get and go mod tidy only. The colors are those of screens.txt; the TUI uses lipgloss.LightDark with tea.RequestBackgroundColor when screens.txt gives a light and a dark value.

decisions.decision: The TUI calls core.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13), D23 of plan 2026-11-13-selection-model: the TUI in cli/internal/tui calls cli/internal/core (the change list, Plan, Apply, Detect) and the catalog reads of cli/internal/source and cli/internal/selection. It does not import cli/internal/cli, and core does not import it. cli/internal/cli parses the arguments and starts the TUI. The TUI builds a change list one key at a time; Review calls core.Plan; Apply calls core.Apply. The TUI gives each answer to core directly, so the prompts of the CLI never run under the TUI (D14 (2) of plan 2026-11-12-catalog-engine). No string literal of cli/internal/tui names a tool: each name, summary, description, category and question text comes from the data, and TestEngineNamesNoTool stays green with no allow entry for cli/internal/tui.
decisions.rejected: Plan 2c moves the code of cli/internal/cli into a shared package.

decisions.decision: No automated tests of the TUI screens.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13): plan 2c adds no automated test of the TUI screens; the user tests the TUI by hand after the landing. Backlog item B29 (P1) holds the tests: golden View strings at 100x25, no teatest. The tests of core come from plan 2026-11-13-selection-model, and test:go, test:repo and test:mac stay the gates. A unit can add a Go unit test of a pure function (for example a truncation or the pack mark) when it helps; it adds no golden file of a screen.
decisions.rejected: Golden View strings in this plan; teatest (a separate experimental module).

decisions.decision: The help modal.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13): the key ? opens a modal help dialog. It lists each key of the current screen, one line for each key, with the full view of the Bubbles help component. esc closes it. The key line at the bottom shows the short view.
decisions.rejected: No spec for ?; the key line only.

decisions.decision: The Detected tab lists only the categories with a proposal.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13), which changes ruling 16 of screens.txt: the left pane of the Detected tab lists only the categories that have a proposal. If nothing is detected, the right pane shows "No tool detected".
decisions.rejected: All the categories, as on the Tools tab.

decisions.decision: Cancel at select.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13): when the user selects a tool with questions, the questions form opens. Cancel in that form also cancels the select: the tool stays [ ], and no change goes on the change list. Cancel in the form of e keeps the old answers, and the tool stays selected. Cancel in a form at Apply stops Apply and keeps the change list (ruling 58 of screens.txt).
decisions.rejected: Keep the select and ask again at Apply.

decisions.decision: Planner assumptions.
decisions.ruling: Assumed by the planner from D1-D6 and screens.txt: (a) the bottom pane of a pack also shows the line Members, as screen 2 of screens.txt does. (b) The repo and Mac categories and their order come from the category data of plan 2026-11-12-catalog-data, not from the script of screens.txt. (c) The TUI has no equivalent of --exclude: a pack is a shortcut, and the user deselects one tool on the Tools tab. (d) The change to the Mac tool git (ruling 44) is in plan 2026-11-12-catalog-data (its D4); plan 2c does not change it. (e) tui and mac tui take the flags of init and mac init without --no-tui, --yes, --answer and --dry-run; they take no names. (f) tui on a repository with no values file stops with code 2 and the message and the hint of the other commands today ("<file> is not there", "run bootstrap init first", select.go:60); mac tui the same with "bootstrap mac init". (g) With no terminal (a.interactive() is false), tui and mac tui stop with code 2 and the hint "use: bootstrap init --no-tui" ("bootstrap mac init --no-tui" on the Mac); init and mac init with no terminal keep the --no-tui path of plan 2026-11-13-selection-model. (h) A terminal smaller than 100x25 at the start: code 2 and the size message of ruling 56 of screens.txt, for tui, mac tui, init and mac init. (i) screens.txt in this folder is a copy of the design artifact Bootstrap TUI Screens (version 47); each unit reads its screens there, and the rulings of this index.json win over it. (j) Each line number in this folder is from main before plans 1a, 1b and 2a; a unit finds the code by the name of its function.

decisions.decision: The release.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13): the release level of bootstrap is MINOR (bootstrap@3.1.0): the commands tui and mac tui are new, and init opens the TUI in a terminal; with no terminal and with --no-tui nothing changes, and the forms of the values file and packs.toml stay. The run records the level and bumps nothing. The user tests the TUI by hand, then tags bootstrap@3.1.0, and the release workflow writes cli/VERSION.
decisions.rejected: MAJOR; a bump of cli/VERSION without a release.

decisions.decision: Units and execution.
decisions.ruling: Ruling of the user (2026-11-13): nine units in nine waves: U1 the shell, U2 the Tools tab, U3 the Packs tab, U4 the Detected tab, U5 the questions form and Apply, U6 the Mac side, U7 the review, U8 the docs, U9 the gates. Execution is teams. Each of U1-U6 changes cli/, so each waits for the unit before it.
decisions.rejected: One unit for the whole TUI.

decisions.decision: Planner assumptions after rulings review round 1.
decisions.ruling: Assumed by the planner from D1-D9 after rulings review round 1: (a) The names: plan 1a is 2026-11-12-catalog-engine, plan 1b is 2026-11-12-catalog-data, plan 2a is 2026-11-13-selection-model, and plan 2c is this plan. (b) The order of the checks of tui and mac tui: the terminal check of D7 (g) first, then the size check of D7 (h), then the values file of D7 (f). (c) mac tui finds macos.toml as each mac command except mac init does: --repo-path, MACOS_SETUP_REPO_PATH, then the current folder; mac tui also takes --repo-path. (d) tui and mac tui on a values file in an old form (no format = 2, or a [packs.*] table) stop with code 2 with the same message and hint as sync and check on that file (D17 h of plan 2a). (e) The clean-target rule of docs/design/cli.md applies to Apply of the TUI: the review names each dirty target, Apply writes nothing, and the TUI keeps the change list. U5 calls the check of that rule in cli/internal/core (D23 of plan 2a, amended 2026-11-13), the same function that the CLI calls. (f) The search of the Tools tab covers the name, the summary, the description and the category, as screen 3 of screens.txt does. (g) If cli/internal/core does not export the package prefixes when U6 runs, U6 exports them from core; the allow entry of TestEngineNamesNoTool for those words moves with the code to the new path, with the same words (D23 of plan 2a).

decisions.decision: init flags, the migration in the TUI, and the own packages.
decisions.ruling: Rulings of the user (2026-11-13) on rulings review round 1: (a) init and mac init in a terminal with --yes, --dry-run or --answer take the --no-tui path, also without --no-tui: these flags come from an agent or a script, and the TUI is for a person. (b) On a values file in an old form, init in a terminal opens the TUI with the migration as one change on the change list, for example "migrate the values file to format 2"; the counter counts it, and the review shows it. Apply writes it with the other changes in one write of the values file (core.Plan and core.Apply of plan 2a). A quit that discards the change list writes nothing, and the next init migrates again. The user cannot remove the migration change from the list. (c) On the Mac, the Detected tab lists the own packages that core.Detect returns (the installed packages that no tool has) in a last category "Own packages", with the [?] marks; space accepts one, and a accepts all, also the own packages, the same as bootstrap mac detect --add (AddPackage items, D16 f of plan 2a).
decisions.rejected: (a) Open the TUI and ignore the flags; (b) write the migration before the TUI opens; (c) leave the own packages out of the TUI.

decisions.decision: Planner assumptions after rulings review round 2.
decisions.ruling: Assumed by the planner from D1-D11 after rulings review round 2: (a) D11 (b) applies to mac init too: on an old-form macos.toml, mac init in a terminal opens the TUI with the migration as one change on the change list. (b) The next command after a sync that passes: on the repo side, MISE_ENV=dev mise run setup (ruling 39 of screens.txt names setup:all, a task that docs/sync/migrate.md retired for setup); on the Mac side, none, because the Mac sync installs the tools itself and prints its own warnings. The string is a constant of cli/internal/tui; it names no tool. (c) The output of the sync: core.Apply takes the stdout and the stderr writers from its caller, as repo.RunWith does today; core still prints nothing of its own. Before Apply, the TUI releases the terminal (the ReleaseTerminal and RestoreTerminal of the Bubble Tea program), so the before script, the sync and mise bootstrap on the Mac write to the terminal; after Apply, the TUI shows "Press a key to go back", then restores the terminal and the main screen. (d) When the user opens the Detected tab again, a proposal that is on the change list shows [+] or [-] from the change list, not [?]. A Detect result that arrives after esc is dropped.

decisions.decision: Planner assumptions after rulings review round 3.
decisions.ruling: Assumed by the planner from D1-D12 after rulings review round 3: (a) If core.Apply of plan 2a takes no stdout and stderr writers when U5 runs, U5 adds them (it owns cli/) and the CLI passes its own writers; nothing else of core.Apply changes. (b) When core.Detect, core.Plan or the clean-target check returns an error value, the TUI shows the error in a modal with a message only (as ruling 26 of screens.txt); any key closes it, and the TUI keeps the change list. (c) The exit code: a quit by the user after the TUI opened is code 0, also after a failed sync; the TUI shows the failure on the screen. Each error before the TUI opens keeps the exit code that the CLI gives for it today (the preflight, the clone, the parse of the values file, a format other than 2, the repository of macos.toml), and the checks of D7 f, g, h and D10 b, d give code 2.

decisions.decision: Planner assumptions after rulings review round 4.
decisions.ruling: Assumed by the planner from D1-D13 after rulings review round 4: (a) The engine has no flag --skip-answer (D15 of plan 1a); D7 (e) and D11 (a) do not name it; an empty --answer <tool>.<key>= is an --answer. (b) The order of the checks of init and mac init: the terminal check, then the flags of D11 (a) and --no-tui (each gives the --no-tui path, also in a small terminal), then the size check of D7 (h), then the migration of D11 (b) in the TUI. (c) On a repository with no values file, init opens the TUI with one change on the change list, "create the values file with base" (ruling 50 of screens.txt): the counter counts it, the review shows it, a quit asks "Discard 1 change? [y/N]", and the user cannot remove it, as the migration of D11 (b).

decisions.decision: Q1: On a light terminal background, should the TUI keep the design's dark-look accent colors on the terminal's own background, or paint the whole 100x25 screen with the design's dark background #15191a?
decisions.ruling: Keep the terminal background (as built) — plain text and titles read on both themes, but the light accent colors (#9be37f, #e3c06b) are weak on white.
decisions.rejected: Paint #15191a behind every cell — the same dark look in both themes, as the design shows, but the TUI ignores the user's terminal theme

decisions.decision: Q2: The long way of a replace (no migrate script, ruling 27) puts two changes on the TUI change list, remove the old tool then add the new one, so the counter goes up by 2, though Edit 6 says each action is one change. Should it be one change?
decisions.ruling: Keep two changes (as built) — they match the two CLI commands (remove tool and add tool), the review can show them as two lines, and undo works per tool.
decisions.rejected: Add an item kind to core (for example a Replace with no script, or a flag on Replace) — one change in the counter and the review, but core's Plan and Apply get a new item kind, which U5 must then handle

decisions.decision: Q3: When a pack is deselected and a selected tool outside the pack needs one of its members, does that member stay, or does the outside tool leave too after the cascade dialog?
decisions.ruling: Member stays only when a required tool needs it; any other outside tool that needs a leaving member leaves too, after the cascade [y/N] (as built) — both clauses apply, and the cascade can actually open.
decisions.rejected: Member stays whenever any selected tool outside the pack needs it — no outside tool ever leaves, so the cascade modal never opens for a pack and the second clause has no effect

decisions.decision: Q4: What does space do on a [~] pack (some members selected): select the missing members, or deselect the pack?
decisions.ruling: Select: one AddPack item that adds the missing members, shown as [+] (as built) — a [~] pack cannot be deselected until it is [x]; the user removes single tools on the Tools tab.
decisions.rejected: Deselect: one RemoveTool item for the selected members, shown as [-] — a [~] pack can only be completed by selecting its missing tools on the Tools tab

decisions.decision: Q5: The Mac scan returns notes from Detection.Notes (for example brew is not installed). Should the TUI Detected tab show them?
decisions.ruling: Show them as dim lines in the bottom pane on a category, and under "No tool detected" — the user learns why a package is missing; it adds lines the design does not show.
decisions.rejected: Drop them — matches the design, but a Mac without brew or mas silently gets fewer proposals

decisions.decision: Q6: Should a (accept all) on the Detected tab also accept the remove proposals (red [?])?
decisions.ruling: Adds only, as built — matches "Same as: bootstrap detect --add", which only adds; red [?] rows still need space one at a time, with the cascade dialog.
decisions.rejected: Also removals — matches the wording "Accept all proposals", but one keypress could open several cascade or locked dialogs in a row

decisions.decision: Q7: Screen 2a shows a counter and a progress bar in the Detecting dialog; core.Detect reports no progress. Should a progress callback be added?
decisions.ruling: Spinner only, as built — no change to core or the scripts runner; the dialog does not match screen 2a.
decisions.rejected: Add a progress callback to core.DetectState and scripts.Runner.Run — the dialog matches the design, but the core and scripts APIs change

decisions.decision: Q8: The wave gate code:lint fails in code:lint:60-bootstrap because the released engine 2.1.0 rejects main's repo/packs.toml in the cache clone (inherited, not this plan). How should the run treat that line for the rest of the run?
decisions.ruling: Treat code:lint:60-bootstrap as inherited from main: count the wave gate green when every other code:lint step passes, record one open gap naming it, and continue — the plan lands; the gap stays open until a 3.x engine release, so the folder is not archived.
decisions.rejected: Stop the run here (STOPPED) until a new engine is released or the clone is fixed; Mark wave 4 failed as the rules say for an unattributed red line
